subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw expose public prime/phase-jitter controls for heartbeat and cron `every` schedules, or keep the current internal heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger as the supported anti-herd behavior?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix changes public config, CLI, protocol, and scheduling semantics; repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces.

options.title: Design narrow phase/stagger controls
options.body: Approve a focused public contract for deterministic phase/stagger on heartbeat and cron `every`, with docs, protocol/schema updates, upgrade proof, and tests; defer or reject prime cadence unless it has separate evidence.

options.title: Keep current behavior only
options.body: Close or downgrade the feature direction after documenting that internal heartbeat phase and cron-expression staggering are the supported anti-herd mechanisms.

options.title: Route through broader scheduling design
options.body: Fold this into the condition/event-trigger scheduling discussion so all cadence, trigger, and jitter semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Design narrow phase/stagger controls
recommendation.body: Approve a focused public contract for deterministic phase/stagger on heartbeat and cron `every`, with docs, protocol/schema updates, upgrade proof, and tests; defer or reject prime cadence unless it has separate evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current routing candidate because of active cron trigger work across the same public scheduler/schema surface.
